meta.what: Net public cost of hosting refugees from Ukraine per host country and year: gross public cost minus taxes and social contributions paid by (working) refugees, plus VAT/excise on their spending where sources or the model include it.
meta.units: EUR bn nominal per calendar year; 2026 = January-August, not annualised; {low, central, high} ~90%. PLN and CZK at ECB annual averages as in refugees.json (PLN 4.6861/4.542/4.3058/4.2397/4.2598; CZK 24.5659/24.0043/25.1198/24.6879/24.2829). No USD conversion needed.

fields.gross_map_now: what the map applies today: round4b.json refugees for its 27 hosts, else refugees.json modelled cost net of flowback2 donor share
fields.gross_revised: only POL, BGR, HRV: new budget evidence found in this round (replaces gross_map_now if adopted)
fields.gross: gross used for net = gross_revised where present, else gross_map_now
fields.revenue: taxes + social contributions (+ VAT/excise) attributable to refugees
fields.revenue_basis: official (ministry figure), official_adjusted (ministry figure for all Ukrainians, minus a no-war counterfactual), official_partial, counts_official_wages_modelled (official employment counts x modelled wage and wedge), modelled (person-years x working-age share x employment rate x 0.5 x average wage x tax wedge + person-years x 3% of GDP per head indirect taxes)
fields.net: gross - revenue; CAN BE NEGATIVE (host budget gained). Range combines gross and revenue uncertainty in quadrature.
fields.net_floored: recommended map series: the 2022-2026 total net is floored at zero and spread over the years with positive net (a country whose total is negative gets zeros)

meta.method: Revenue official where a ministry has published it (CZE MPSV from CSSZ contribution records; POL Ministry of Finance from PIT/ZUS/NFZ registers, all Ukrainian citizens, minus pre-war Ukrainians grown with wages and +4%/yr headcount; LTU Ministry of Social Security; MDA Economic Council). DEU: Federal Employment Agency counts of Ukrainians in contributory jobs above the February 2022 level x EUR 2,300/month (1,900-2,800) x 51% wedge (45-55%), minijobs x EUR 160/month, plus indirect taxes 2.5% (1.5-4%) of GDP per head per person-year. Everyone else modelled: revenue = PY x 0.62 (working-age share; 0.65 USA/CAN/AUS, 0.55 MDA) x employment rate (EMN-OECD 2024 table, OECD 2025 press figures; guesses marked D) x 0.5 (0.42-0.58) of national average wage x total tax wedge (income tax + employee + employer contributions as share of gross wage at ~67% AW) + PY x 3% (1.95-4.05%) of GDP per head for VAT/excise (Czech MPSV measured 2.9-3.7%). USA: federal taxes and payroll only (wedge 22%, no sales tax) because the USA gross covers federal spending only.

recommendation_floor: Use net cost, floored at zero on each country's 2022-2026 total (field net_floored), in both the net-shift and the cost view; keep gross and revenue in More details and show a negative total as a note ('hosting paid for itself for the budget: +X'). Reasons: (1) the method counts changes against a no-war world; without the war neither the hosting costs nor the refugees' taxes exist, so the war's effect on the host budget is the net; (2) a net fiscal gain comes from refugees' own work and is not money moved toward Russia, so it must not show as a pro-Russia shift on a single-axis map; (3) revenue figures are mostly modelled, include pension contributions that create future pension claims, and are measured on a wider scope (all levels of government) than several gross figures (central government only), so negative values are less certain than positive ones; (4) flooring each year separately is not recommended: it keeps early deficits and drops later surpluses (Czechia would show +0.69 instead of 0).

poland_check.beneficiaries: PESEL UKR numbers issued 2022-2023: 1,736,600 (government report). Eurostat temporary protection stock peaked at 1.37m (Sep 2022) and was 0.96m in Dec 2022 after the PESEL clean-up; person-years 2022 = 0.91m (refugees.json). 474,125 people used state collective accommodation in 2022; 190.6k refugee pupils at end-2022; 500+ child benefit paid for about 0.3m children.
poland_check.spending_2022: Aid Fund (Fundusz Pomocy, BGK) spending on Ukrainians per the Ministry of Finance (answer to interpellation 15498, 10 Apr 2026): PLN 11.3bn in 2022, 8.9bn in 2023, 8.1bn in 2024 (NIK: over PLN 11bn in 2022). The PLN 13.87bn (2022) and 14.78bn (2023) in the government's 'Polska Pomoc Ukrainie 2022-2023' are total Fund spending, which also funds tasks outside Poland and food security; that is the source of the radiospacja.pl figures used in refugees.json and round4b. Named 2022 items: host payments PLN 40/day (3.94bn over 2022-23), collective accommodation (3.55bn over 2022-23), 500+ for refugees 1.74bn, other family benefits 0.29bn, one-off PLN 300 0.39bn (2022-23), education support to local governments 1.59bn; these were all paid from the Fund, so 'Fund plus 800+' (round4b low) double-counts the child benefit.
poland_check.verdict: round4b's central PLN 33bn (EUR 7.0bn) for 2022 is about 2.9 times the Fund's refugee spending and leans on modelled OECD (EUR 8.4bn) and Kiel estimates and on the government's PLN 90bn for 2022-23, which covers all humanitarian and economic help, not hosting. Recommended 2022: PLN 11.3 / 13.6 / 18.0bn = EUR 2.4 / 2.9 / 3.8bn (central = Fund x 1.2 for local-government and ministry spending outside the Fund; high allows total Fund spending plus local costs). Poland 2022-2026 falls from EUR 24.0bn to 10.8bn (6.6-14.5).

overlaps: This file replaces nothing by itself; it gives the builder a net series for the existing 'Refugee hosting' part. Gross figures are round4b.json and refugees.json unchanged (except the proposed POL/BGR/HRV revisions). Revenue is not counted anywhere else in the map: no part counts refugees' taxes, wages or remittances. Remittances from refugees to Ukraine are not in this file. Germany's gross (Buergergeld outturn) is already net of benefit cuts when refugees work, and revenue counts only taxes, so that effect is not counted twice. Poland's revenue is the change against a no-war path of pre-war Ukrainian workers, so pre-war labour migrants' taxes are not credited to refugees. Czechia's MPSV revenue counts only Ukrainians first insured after 24 Feb 2022. Donor share (flowback2.json) applies to gross only; Poland's revised gross is Fund spending, which excludes UN/NGO donor money, so no donor share should be taken off it, and Bulgaria's revised gross is the government programme (EU-funded part kept, as round4b does), so the flowback2 donor share should not be applied to it either. eu_funded in round4b is unaffected.
notes: Builder bug to check: build_data.py applies the flowback2 donor share (lines ~410-419) and then apply_audit() overwrites refugee_years for every round4b host (lines ~1495-1502). For MDA that is intended; for POL, ROU, SVK and CZE the donor share (central 6%, 20%, 15%, 6%) is silently dropped while refugee_donor_share stays in the record.

refugees.json calibrates k on Poland's Fund totals 13.87/14.78 (EUR 2.96bn/3.25bn) for 2022-2023; the refugee-only figures are 11.3/8.9 (EUR 2.41bn/1.96bn). Re-running the calibration with those would lower k a little (Poland's 2023 k falls from 0.145 to 0.087).
Revenue includes pension contributions (largest single item in CZ and PL). They are real budget income now but create pension claims later; another reason not to let net go below zero on the map.

Scope mismatches: USA gross covers federal spending only, so USA revenue is federal only. Spain's and France's gross leave out health and schools (round4b caveat) while revenue covers all levels; their net is biased low.

Canada, Czechia, Slovakia, Romania, Portugal, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia and Moldova have negative central totals (hosting paid for itself for the budget); the UK, the USA and Spain turn negative from 2025 and are small over the whole period.
